clue.text: 500 university Fellows not working

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500
F is the abbreviation for Fellow, doubled as FF for the plural

explanation.surface: A tally of five hundred college Fellows who are idle or unemployed.
explanation.definitionFit: Duff is British slang for broken or useless, so a duff gadget is one that is not functioning.

clue.text: Drank heavily on the way up to warehouse

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters of the drinking word are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to tope is to drink alcohol to excess, so drank heavily gives the past tense

explanation.surface: Someone drank heavily while travelling up to a storage building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way up' turns TOPED, an old word for drank heavily, backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storehouse where goods are kept before distribution, a synonym for warehouse.

clue.text: Imagines cooler cities cut it

parts.note: a fan is a device that cools the air

indicators.note: cut says the following word is removed from the word before it

parts.note: taken as written, the letters removed

explanation.surface: Someone pictures cooler cities and decides that is quite enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' takes IT out of CITIES, leaving CIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to think or suppose it, so fancies is a verb synonym of imagines.

clue.text: Energy-producing US state alternatively provided Italy with carbon

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
or introduces an alternative
if means provided that
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A list of ingredients for an energy source: an American state, Italy and carbon.
explanation.definitionFit: Calorific describes food or fuel that yields heat or calories, the units of dietary energy.

clue.text: Head guy sacks one cook

indicators.note: sacks means dismisses, so the letter for one is thrown out of the word

parts.note: a chief is the man at the head of a group
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The boss fires one of the kitchen staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacks' removes I (one) from CHIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook, especially one in charge of a kitchen.

clue.text: Feller found by someone sleeping topless

indicators.note: topless means the word loses its first letter, which in a down clue is at the top

parts.note: a slumberer is a person asleep

explanation.surface: A man discovered by a sleeper who happens to be shirtless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops the first letter S from SLUMBERER. 'Feller' looks like slang for a fellow but means one who fells trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A lumberer cuts down trees for timber, which is exactly what a feller of trees does.

clue.text: Trip over Grampian's premier hill-range

indicators.note: over means the journey word lies over, so around, the next letter

parts.note: a ride is a short journey or trip

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter of Grampian is used

explanation.surface: An outing across the highest hills of the Grampian region in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts RIDE around G, the first letter of Grampian ('premier'). The Grampians are a Scottish mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow stretch of high ground, effectively a line of hills.

clue.text: Waste from British beer Belgium leaves for France

indicators.note: leaves for says the first country departs and the second takes its place

parts.note: bitter is a well-hopped British ale
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: A lament that British beer is pouring out of Belgium into France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves for' replaces B (Belgium) in BITTER with FR (France). Bitter is a classic British pub ale.
explanation.definitionFit: To fritter money or time is to squander it bit by bit, a synonym of waste.

clue.text: Chortle at funny little princess

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An invitation to laugh at a comic young royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' rearranges the letters of CHORTLE AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Charlotte is the young daughter of the Prince and Princess of Wales, a British royal child.

clue.text: Contacted a Weasley by phone for some Hogwarts equipment

indicators.note: by phone suggests something heard rather than seen, so the words are said out loud

parts.note: to have called someone is to have contacted them; Ron Weasley is Harry Potter's friend in the novels

explanation.surface: Someone telephoned one of the Weasley family about kit needed for a Hogwarts class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by phone' says CALLED RON is spoken, which sounds like the answer. Hogwarts is the wizarding school in Harry Potter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils at the wizarding school brew potions in a large metal pot, part of their required kit.

clue.text: Theatrical foundation to criticise piece of soap

parts.note: to pan a show is to review it harshly
soap is sold as a cake, a solid block

explanation.surface: A make-up base for the stage is attacked as no better than a bar of soap.
explanation.definitionFit: Pancake is a thick, solid stage make-up applied as a base layer, a foundation used by actors.

clue.text: Admire a developed EU island

indicators.note: developed means worked into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fan of a European island that has been built up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges the letters of ADMIRE A.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a Portuguese island in the Atlantic, so part of the European Union.

clue.text: Play with something of little value

definitions.meaning: to toy or fiddle idly with something
a thing of small importance or worth

explanation.surface: Toying with a worthless bauble.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with someone is to toy with them, and a trifle is also a trinket of no importance.

clue.text: Fashion dept sale raised support

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters are reformed

explanation.surface: A fashion department's sale has drummed up some backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like the store department, but it is the verb that rearranges DEPT SALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedestal is the base on which a statue or column stands, holding it up high.

clue.text: Wilderness of chopped up dead trees

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as on family trees

indicators.note: chopped up means cut into pieces and rearranged, a natural fit for trees

explanation.surface: A barren landscape made of felled dead trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped up' rearranges D (dead) with TREES.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert is a barren, uninhabited region, the sense of wilderness.

clue.text: Jihadist ancestors covering miles perhaps

indicators.note: covering means the two words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Militant forebears who travelled great distances.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in jihaDIST ANCEStors, held by 'covering'.
explanation.definitionFit: Miles are one example of a measured length, the kind of span between places.

clue.text: Protest march about renegade politician?

parts.note: a demo is a demonstration or protest march
C, from circa, means about
a rat is a deserter or turncoat

explanation.surface: A demonstration targeting a politician who changed sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: an American party member.
explanation.definitionFit: A Democrat belongs to one of the two main US parties, an example of a politician.

clue.text: Unavailable because engaged

definitions.meaning: said of a seat or toilet already in use
busy, taken up with some task

explanation.surface: Someone cannot come because they are betrothed or busy.
explanation.definitionFit: A taken room is not free, and a busy person is taken up with work: both senses of the word.

clue.text: Practise on last means of transport

parts.note: re means on or concerning
a hearse carries a body on its final journey

explanation.surface: Someone trains using the final vehicle available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last means of transport' sounds like the final bus home, but it is the funeral carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehearse is to practise a play, speech or piece before performing it.

clue.text: He's temporarily assigned support with central fees

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it

indicators.note: central means only the middle letters of fees are taken

explanation.surface: A worker on a short-term posting gets backing and middling pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A secondee is a worker lent for a fixed period to another post or organisation.

clue.text: Fall apart when tummy noise follows onset of colic

indicators.note: follows puts the tummy noise after the opening letter
onset means beginning, so just the first letter of colic

parts.note: a rumble is the sound of a hungry stomach

explanation.surface: A baby's colic begins with stomach gurgles and everything goes wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To crumble is to break into small fragments, or figuratively to collapse or disintegrate.

clue.text: Tight spot in drug brawl? On the contrary

indicators.note: on the contrary reverses the order the clue implies, so the fight comes before the drug

parts.note: a scrap is a fight or brawl
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Trouble at a fight over drugs, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drug brawl' would put E before SCRAP; 'On the contrary' swaps them so SCRAP comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament, a difficult situation like a tight spot.

clue.text: Incontinent drunken men cause of memory loss

indicators.note: drunken means the letters reel about and are rearranged

parts.note: the word splits as in continent, and the continent is Asia

explanation.surface: Drunk men unable to control themselves cause blackouts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incontinent' splits as 'in continent': strictly, 'drunken' rearranges MEN into MNE, which goes inside ASIA, the continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is a medical condition in which a person loses the ability to remember.

clue.text: Overly praised mature journalist penning article

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the article sits inside

parts.note: adult means grown up or mature
a is the indefinite article
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A seasoned reporter writing a piece got heaped with too much praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' means enclosing, as sheep are penned. ED, short for editor, is a standard crossword journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: To adulate is to flatter or admire excessively, so adulated means praised too much.

clue.text: Suffered from a charcuterie upset?

indicators.note: upset means turned upside down, so in a down clue the letters read bottom to top

parts.note: a charcuterie is a shop selling cooked meats, like a deli

explanation.surface: Someone fell ill after eating at a cold-meats counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns DELI backwards, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To have ailed is to have been unwell or in pain, a synonym of suffered.

clue.text: Bum from Home Counties harbouring nasty smell

indicators.note: harbouring means sheltering, so one thing holds the other

parts.note: the counties around London lie in the South East, SE
pong is British slang for a stink

explanation.surface: A smelly vagrant from the area around London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the English counties surrounding London, in the South East. 'Bum' is the verb meaning to cadge, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To bum is to cadge or scrounge, and to sponge is to live off others the same way.

clue.text: Meeting seven television hosts

indicators.note: hosts means holds within, so the words contain the answer

explanation.surface: A gathering hosted by seven TV channels.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is held in sEVEN Television, signalled by 'hosts'.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an organised occasion such as a race meeting or gathering.

clue.text: Fox film regularly receives 2 Oscars

indicators.note: receives means the picked letters take in the others
regularly means every other letter of film is taken

parts.note: Oscar is O in the radio alphabet, so two of them give OO

explanation.surface: A movie about a fox picks up two Academy Awards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fox' is the verb meaning to baffle, not the animal; 'regularly' takes alternate letters of film.
explanation.definitionFit: To fox someone is to baffle or trick them, a synonym of the verb to fool.

clue.text: Australian mate brings in trainee worker at last

indicators.note: brings in means the mate's word takes the letter inside it

parts.note: cobber is Australian slang for a friend
L stands for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: An Aussie friend finally brings in a new apprentice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at last' looks like 'finally', but a last is a foot-shaped shoemaker's block.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler mends shoes, working them on a last, the model of a foot.

clue.text: Manage to look after maiden, perhaps

indicators.note: after puts the looking word behind the cricket term

parts.note: a maiden is one kind of over in cricket, one with no runs scored
to see is to look

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep an eye on a young girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' looks like a girl, but in cricket a maiden is an over of six balls without a run.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee is to supervise or be in charge of something, a synonym of manage.

clue.text: Press on spring flowering plant

parts.note: to press on is to hurry or speed
a well is a spring of water

explanation.surface: Pushing down on a blooming plant in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell, or veronica, is a small wild plant with blue flowers.

clue.text: Tangy starters of tomato and Roquefort tortellini

indicators.note: starters means the opening letters of each following word are taken; the answer also sitting inside the word starters is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A restaurant menu offers sharp-flavoured starters of tomato and cheese pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starters of' takes the first letters of the four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tart has a sharp, sour taste, as tangy food does.
